title: Conflict refusals name the observed version on the wire; the seat mission retries once at it
description:
SPIDR child B of task-5f5d873e72b546d4a30942bea5c80b97 (leaf; no sibling dependency). Filed by architect-16a01670 2026-09-04, measured at main 68eb1c5d.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: every `EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT` refusal on HTTP `/command` and on the MCP command wire carries the expected AND observed versions, and the seat mission tells the seat what to do with them. Also the mission's seat-facing read facts (graph_get payload roster, no-write-tool line). Nothing else of the parent.

MEASURED (re-measure before planning):
- The store already computes the observed version: packages/store/src/store-digests.ts:181-193 `expectedVersionConflictResultBytes(expectedVersion, observedVersion)` writes `{code, expectedVersion, observedVersion, version}` into the decision's `resultBytes`.
- TWO daemon commit paths drop it: apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts:156-168 `decided()` refuses `refuse(request.kind, response.decision.resultCode, "DURABLE_STORE")` (a `decodeResult(decision.resultBytes)` helper exists at :102); apps/daemon/src/work/work-claim-services.ts commitAccepted (:111-112) refuses the same way. Both hold the `CommandDecisionRecord` with `resultBytes` at the refusal site - DECODE the store's bytes, never recompute the version.
- The wire: apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-dispatch.ts:34-46 `DomainRefusal(code, layer, detail, httpStatus)`; :97-103 `decisionOf` throws it with `detail = outcome.error === null ? outcome.code : outcome.error.code`; :117-122 the frame is `{ outcome: \"REFUSED\", refusal: { code, detail, httpStatus, layer } }` and the MCP command wire (mcp-dispatch-port dispatchCommandBytes) serialises the same object. `detail` is an EXISTING string field, so the versions ride in it with NO shape change: `detail = \"EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT expectedVersion=<n> observedVersion=<m>\"`. A structured `details` key was rejected at plan time: 11 control-room exact-key REFUSED decoders (apps/control-room/src/live/live-*.ts, v2/goals/gate1-refusal.ts) plus the generated client pin the key roster - that is a separate row if ever wanted. Refusal outcome shapes (WorkClaimRefused, BootstrapRequestRefused: {advisoryOnly, authority, code, error, kind, ok, refusedBy}) are pinned by in-package golden tests - carry the versions through the EXISTING `error: RuntimeError | null` slot (registry row packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-error-registry.ts:101 declares NO required detail keys today; either declare `expectedVersion`/`observedVersion` there with its pins, or render the detail string at the refusal site and keep `error` as is - architect decides and states why) rather than adding a key.
- Mission: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts:117-122 tells the seat expectedVersion = claimAggregateVersion from work_get_context; it says nothing about a conflict. `graph_get` accepts EXACTLY `{ projectId }` (apps/daemon/src/planning/graph-query.ts:120 ALLOWED_BODY_KEYS) - the seat guessed shapes and got INPUT_INVALID. `grep -c memory apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts` = 0: the 'record a durable memory' instruction the seat reported is NOT in moe-next's mission (a seat in a project directory reads that project's own CLAUDE.md) - parent clause (e) closes as measured-absent; this row adds one mission sentence: the seat has no file-write tool, it reports instead of writing memories.

FEATURE: (1) both commit paths turn a store conflict into a refusal whose wire `refusal.detail` is exactly `EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT expectedVersion=<n> observedVersion=<m>` (decoded from resultBytes; if the bytes do not decode, detail stays the bare code - never invented). (2) Mission text: on EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT read observedVersion from the refusal detail and retry ONCE at that version, then stop and report; graph_get payload is exactly {projectId}; no file-write tool line. (3) A scripted seat double over the REAL MCP wire proves it: claim -> planted conflict -> release succeeds on the single retry, and the decision ledger shows exactly one `command.expected-version-rejected` record for the run (the planted one), not seven.
definitionOfDone: HTTP `/command` test on one bootstrap kind and MCP command-wire test on `work.release`: a stale expectedVersion yields `outcome: "REFUSED"`, `refusal.code = "EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT"`, `refusal.layer = "DURABLE_STORE"`, and `refusal.detail` matching /^EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT expectedVersion=\d+ observedVersion=\d+$/ with the observed value equal to the aggregate's real version (asserted by reading the store, not the request); undecodable resultBytes leave detail = the bare code (test plants corrupt bytes).

No wire-shape change: `git diff --stat` at completion touches no file under apps/control-room/src/live/ or packages/control-room-client/, and the REFUSED frame's key roster {code, detail, httpStatus, layer} is asserted unchanged in the dispatch test; in-package refusal-outcome goldens stay green or are updated only for the `error` slot.

Mission-text test asserts the three new sentences verbatim (retry once at observedVersion then report; graph_get payload is exactly {projectId}; no file-write tool - report instead of writing memories) and that no sentence mentions writing a memory.

Seat-double e2e over the REAL MCP wire (apps/daemon test with a real store, or tests/e2e/foundation): claim -> planted conflict -> one retry at the observed version -> RELEASED; the decision ledger for the run has exactly one `command.expected-version-rejected` record (the planted one) - asserted by reading the ledger.
Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (root, if packages/contracts is touched), `pnpm test:security` (if the registry is touched).
taskRails: NO WIRE-SHAPE CHANGE: the versions travel in the existing `refusal.detail` string; adding a key to the REFUSED frame is forbidden here (11 exact-key decoders + generated client).
DECODE, NEVER RECOMPUTE: the observed version comes from the store's resultBytes; a daemon-computed version would authenticate nothing.

Refusals carry a stable code AND a layer asserted by a test; mutate the production surface to prove each failure arm goes red (global rail 1). <=250 physical lines per production source, hard stop 400.

implementationPlan.description: LEDGER TESTS FIRST (red). (a) apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-durability.test.ts: the DURABLE_STORE conflict arm at ~:318-335 (stale expectedVersion on a bootstrap kind after project.register, head at version 1) gains: `expect(outcome.error).not.toBeNull()`, `expect(outcome.error?.code).toBe("EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT")`, `expect(outcome.error?.details).toEqual({ actualVersion: 1, expectedVersion: <the stale number the arm sends> })` - the actual value asserted by reading `readDurableLedger(store, PROJECT_ID).aggregates.get(PROJECT_ID)?.currentVersion`, never copied from the request. Add a sibling arm that plants CORRUPT resultBytes on the decision (drive the conflict, then overwrite the stored decision's result bytes through the store's own test seam if one exists, else construct a `CommandDecisionRecord` fixture with `resultBytes = encoder.encode("not json")` and call the exported `decided`-equivalent through `runBootstrapCommand` with a fake store) and asserts `error === null` and `code === "EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT"` (bare code, nothing invented). Note the CORE_REDUCER arm at :225-231 is a DIFFERENT layer (core reducer refusal) and stays untouched. (b) apps/daemon/src/work/work-claim-services.test.ts: the three DURABLE_STORE conflict arms at :132, :155, :179 gain the same `error.code` + `error.details` assertions ({actualVersion: <real version read back from the store>, expectedVersion: <stale>}). Run both files from apps/daemon: `pnpm exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/bootstrap/bootstrap-durability.test.ts src/work/work-claim-services.test.ts` - RED on the new assertions only; quote the failing lines.

That arm is green today (vacuously); step 6 drill (6) makes it load-bearing by making conflictError synthesize a version on undecodable bytes.

(b) work-claim-services.test.ts: added `expectConflictNamesObservedVersion(outcome, item, staleVersion)` helper reading `store.getAggregateVersion(aggregateIdFor(item))` for the actual, wired into all three DURABLE_STORE arms (claim takeover :154, renewal :178, release :203). Imported `type WorkClaimOutcome`.

MEASURED BLOCKER FOR STEP 2 (plan correction, no scope change): the plan's step-2 recipe `createRuntimeError({code:"EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT", details:{actualVersion, expectedVersion}})` DOES NOT WORK. runtime-error-factory.ts `sourceAccepted` (:78-85) returns false when the row declares validSources and the input has no `source` key; the factory then falls back to UNKNOWN_ERROR_DESCRIPTOR with EMPTY_DETAILS. Registry row :101-103 declares `srcs("GOAL","GRAPH_REVISION","NODE_RUN","PLANNING_RUN","PROJECT")`, so no-source => `code:"UNKNOWN_ERROR", details:{}` - the wire would read `detail = "UNKNOWN_ERROR"`, a silent fail-open of the whole feature. Proven by probe (packages/contracts/src/runtime/__probe.test.ts, deleted in the same command): `expected { code: 'UNKNOWN_ERROR', details: {} }` with no source vs `{ code: "EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT", details: { actualVersion: 1, expectedVersion: 0 } }` with `source: {aggregate:"PROJECT", state:"READY"}`.

Claiming a lifecycle source would invent daemon truth (the daemon has read no aggregate STATE at the refusal site, and a work-claim aggregate `work/<id>` is not a RuntimeAggregate at all). Step 2 will therefore follow the EXISTING in-repo precedent for exactly this situation - apps/daemon/src/http/http-command-ingress.ts:49-70 `MISMATCH_ROW`/`DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH`, which projects the registry row VERBATIM (recoveryCategory, recoveryCommands, retryability, transport from `lookupRuntimeError`) with `truthClass: "OBSERVED"` and builds `details` itself. Values are bounded to `Number.isSafeInteger` numbers decoded from the store's resultBytes, mirroring the factory's own `safeScalar`; anything else => error null / bare code. packages/contracts stays untouched, per plan.

Peer dirt noted, not touched: scripts/up.ps1, scripts/watch.ps1, .moe/messages/*, .moe/tasks/*, apps/daemon/src/goals/*.test.ts. bootstrap-durability.test.ts already had a peer edit (14+/6- at session start) - my arms were added alongside it, nothing reverted.

implementationPlan.description: LEDGERS DECODE THE STORE'S BYTES (green). (a) apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-ledger.ts `decided()` (:156-168): when `response.decision.effectDisposition !== "EFFECTS_COMMITTED"` and `resultCode === "EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT"`, decode `response.decision.resultBytes` with the existing `decodeResult` (:102 path, decodeBoundedJsonBytes) and, when it is a plain object carrying numeric `expectedVersion` and `observedVersion` (the store's own names, packages/store/src/store-digests.ts:181-193), return `refuse(request.kind, resultCode, "DURABLE_STORE", createRuntimeError({ code: "EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT", details: { actualVersion: observedVersion, expectedVersion } }))` - `refuse` already takes `error: RuntimeError | null` (:111-126); any other resultCode or undecodable bytes keep today's `refuse(kind, resultCode, "DURABLE_STORE")` with error null. (b) apps/daemon/src/work/work-claim-services.ts: give `refuse()` (:57-66) an optional fourth parameter `error: RuntimeError | null = null` (the exact key roster {advisoryOnly, authority, code, error, kind, ok, refusedBy} is unchanged - `error` already exists); if `WorkClaimRefused.error` is typed as literal `null` in work-claim-contracts.ts widen it to `RuntimeError | null` (type-only); `commitAccepted` (:111-112) mirrors (a) using the SAME small helper - extract `conflictError(decision: CommandDecisionRecord): RuntimeError | null` into bootstrap-ledger.ts (exported) and import it in work-claim-services.ts so the decode lives once. The registry row (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-error-registry.ts:101) already requires exactly these two detail keys, so `createRuntimeError` keeps them; do NOT touch packages/contracts. TWO MEASURED DEVIATIONS FROM THE STEP TEXT, both forced, neither widening scope:

(1) `createRuntimeError` REPLACED BY A VERBATIM REGISTRY PROJECTION. The step said `createRuntimeError({code:"EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT", details:{actualVersion, expectedVersion}})`. That call returns `{code:"UNKNOWN_ERROR", details:{}}` - proven by probe in step 1. Cause: runtime-error-factory.ts `sourceAccepted` (:78-85) returns `descriptor.validSources.length === 0` when the input has no `source` key, and registry row :101-103 declares five valid sources; the factory then falls back to UNKNOWN_ERROR_DESCRIPTOR. Shipping that would have put `detail = "UNKNOWN_ERROR"` on the wire - a silent fail-open of the entire feature that the step-3 regex would then have had to be written around. Supplying a `source` was rejected: the commit seam has read no aggregate STATE when the store reports the conflict, and a work-claim aggregate (`work/<id>`) is not a RuntimeAggregate at all, so naming one invents daemon truth. Instead the row is projected VERBATIM via `lookupRuntimeError("EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT")` - code, recoveryCategory, recoveryCommands, retryability, transport and truthClass ALL from the registry, registryVersion from RUNTIME_ERROR_REGISTRY_VERSION, nextAllowedCommands from EMPTY_NEXT_ALLOWED_COMMANDS - with only `details` built locally. This is the EXISTING in-repo precedent for exactly this situation: apps/daemon/src/http/http-command-ingress.ts:49-70 (`MISMATCH_ROW`/`DISTRIBUTION_MISMATCH`), whose comment names the same fail-closed gate. packages/contracts is UNTOUCHED, as the step required.

(2) NEW FILE apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-conflict-error.ts (76 lines) INSTEAD of adding ~40 lines to bootstrap-ledger.ts. bootstrap-ledger.ts was already 291 lines; inlining would have taken it past 330, well over the <=250 target the task rail sets. Per global rail 2, a per-file cap is fixed by splitting. `conflictError` is RE-EXPORTED from bootstrap-ledger.ts so the step's named import path still resolves, and work-claim-services.ts imports it from the module directly. The decode lives ONCE, which was the step's actual requirement.

CODE. `conflictError(decision: CommandDecisionRecord): RuntimeError | null` fails closed at four gates, each returning null (bare code, nothing invented): resultCode is not EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT; `decodeBoundedJsonBytes(decision.resultBytes)` not ok; decoded value is not a non-array object; either version is not a non-negative safe integer (`versionOf` mirrors the factory's own `safeScalar` bound, so a float/string/NaN/nested object cannot reach the wire). Field marriage is documented at the one place it happens: the store calls the head it saw `observedVersion` (store-digests.ts:181-193), the runtime error registry calls the same number `actualVersion` (registry :103) - decoded, never recomputed.

(a) bootstrap-ledger.ts `decided()` now passes `conflictError(response.decision)` as the 4th arg to the existing `refuse(kind, code, refusedBy, error = null)` (:111-126, the param already existed). (b) work-claim-services.ts `refuse()` gained the same optional 4th param `error: RuntimeError | null = null` and `commitAccepted` passes `conflictError(response.decision)`. `WorkClaimRefused.error` was ALREADY typed `RuntimeError | null` (work-claim-services.ts:46) - the plan's risk (b) "may be typed as literal null" measured FALSE, no widening needed and work-claim-contracts.ts is untouched. The exact key roster {advisoryOnly, authority, code, error, kind, ok, refusedBy} is unchanged on both refusal shapes.
